historical_growth.growth_divergence_warning: Equity CAGR (12.1% 5y) is more than double revenue CAGR (5.4% 5y) and diverges >30% from 5y EPS CAGR (6.6%). Book value is a poor growth proxy here: SGX retains ~40% of earnings into investment securities and goodwill (Scientific Beta, BidFX, MaxxTrader), so book compounds faster than the fee base. Revenue 5y CAGR selected.
historical_growth.notes: Owner-FCF series (reported FCF - SBC - interest income): FY2020 561.2, FY2021 484.7, FY2022 521.1, FY2023 346.4, FY2024 493.0, FY2025 718.7 (S$m). Owner-FCF CAGRs track reported FCF closely (SBC ~1.3% of revenue, not growing faster than cash flow). The series is noisy because OCF swings with clearing receivables/payables and committed-cash movements (FY2023 trough, FY2025 peak); the FY2025 endpoint flatters the 3y and 5y FCF CAGRs. FY2025 revenue +11.3% (FY2024 +3.1%) on record derivatives volumes and a 28% rise in securities ADV.

scenario_narratives.base: Mid-single-digit compounding of a regulated-monopoly fee stream: Singapore listing/trading/clearing plus a global multi-asset derivatives franchise (equity index, FX, commodities). FY2026 benefits from strong 2025 equities activity; growth then fades from ~6% to 3% with pre-SBC EBITDA margin ~62%. Treasury income drifts lower with rates but volume growth offsets it.
scenario_narratives.bull: Equity-market reform succeeds and FX becomes a second growth leg: revenue 7-11% early, margin to 65% on operating leverage, terminal growth 3%.
scenario_narratives.bear: Volume mean reversion plus rate cuts: FY2025's record derivatives volumes and the treasury-income spread both normalise, competition in Asian index futures limits pricing, revenue roughly flat for two years then ~3%, margin 58%.

valuation_philosophy.summary: SGX is valued as an operating fee business on owner FCF at an SGD cost of equity of 7%, with its surplus investment portfolio (cash, bonds, FVPL/FVOCI securities) added at fair value and its clearing-fund contributions excluded as encumbered. The terminal value is capped at 20x FCF, which binds in every scenario because Gordon at 7%/2.5% is ~22.8x. Even the bull case sits below the market price: the price implies either sustained high-single-digit growth beyond the bull path or a discount rate well below 7% (see required_return_table).
key_risks_to_valuation: Corpus stale: FY2026 results (June 2026 year-end) and the Dec-2025 balance sheet are not extracted; FY2026 is modelled, not observed
Treasury income on margin collateral (S$126m net FY2025, ~9% of revenue) is directly exposed to SGD/USD short rates
Derivatives volumes (equity index, FX, commodities) are cyclical and FY2025 was a record year
Competition in Asian index futures (HKEX MSCI China A50, NSE IX GIFT City) and regulatory fee pressure from MAS
Unquoted FVPL debt securities (S$449m) and FVOCI equity stakes (S$184m) are carried at fair value in the bridge without haircut

inputs.share_count_basis: Fully diluted: FY2025 weighted-average diluted count 1,075.232m (basic 1,069.960m + 5.272m performance-share/DLTI awards; the FY2024 convertible-bond dilution of 21.5m fell away when the bonds were repaid in FY2025, S$349.6m). Held FLAT because SBC is expensed in the flows; SGX repurchases shares (S$26.3m FY2025) to cover award vesting, so the flat count is funded.
inputs.cash_note: Cash = unrestricted cash per cash-flow statement S$919.3m + quoted bonds at FVOCI S$377.6m (current, interest-bearing; their S$5.5m interest is in the stripped interest income). EXCLUDED: S$171.4m cash committed to the SGX-DC and Securities Clearing Funds and S$39.3m NEMS cash - these are default-waterfall resources SGX must hold, not distributable. Debt = medium-term notes only (USD 250m 1.234% due Sep-2026, SGD 300m 3.45% due Feb-2027); lease liabilities (S$65.2m) excluded under lease treatment (B). FY2025 AR notes 11, 15, 26.
inputs.sbc_source: FY2025 AR consolidated cash-flow statement, 'Share-based payment expense' add-back S$17,740k (FY2024 S$20,978k). No net-share-settlement tax line: SGX settles awards from treasury shares bought on market, so equity-award taxes are 0.
inputs.wacc_rationale: SGD build: 10y SGS ~2.3%, beta 0.75 (SGX's 5y beta to the STI is low; a vertically integrated listing/trading/clearing monopoly), ERP 6.0% -> cost of equity ~6.8%, rounded to 7.0%. Net cash, so WACC = cost of equity. Same 7.0% in every scenario: risk is charged in the scenario flows (volume normalisation, treasury-income compression), not a second time in the discount rate.
inputs.lease_treatment: Treatment (B), leases as operating cost: lease cash (FY2025 principal S$23.2m + interest S$2.6m = S$25.8m, 1.88% of revenue) charged via lease_cost_pct_path; lease liabilities excluded from net debt; da_pct_path is D&A ex right-of-use depreciation (total D&A S$84.9m less est. ~S$19.5m ROU depreciation = ~S$65m, 4.8% of revenue).
inputs.nci_treatment: Immaterial: NCI share of profit S$0.1m FY2025 and the remaining NCI was bought out in FY2025 (S$10.3m). Flows are effectively attributable.
inputs.notes: MODEL: owner-FCF DCF (component route) + non-US adaptations. Routing: SGX is a vertically integrated exchange operator - listing, trading, clearing, depository, data/indices - whose value is an operating fee stream. It is not a deposit taker: clearing-member margin collateral is held in trust OFF balance sheet, and SGX earns a net 'treasury income on collateral balances' spread (S$126.1m FY2025) that is reported inside operating revenue and is kept in the flows as an operating, rate-sensitive revenue line (bear case compresses it). Its own investment portfolio IS non-operating: interest income (S$37.1m) is stripped from FCF and the cash/bonds sit in net cash; FVPL debt/equity securities (S$463.7m), unquoted FVOCI equity stakes (S$183.5m) and associates/JVs (S$31.6m) go in the equity_bridge, and their fair-value gains (S$42.7m FY2025, S$84.5m FY2024 in 'other income') are excluded from the flows. EBITDA margin path is PRE-SBC (reported EBITDA S$827.8m is after S$17.7m SBC in staff cost, so 845.5/1370.6 = 61.7%). Revenue base is gross operating revenue (S$1,370.6m); transaction-based expenses (S$72.5m) sit inside the EBITDA margin. Reported FCF S$773.6m is flattered by a S$172m receivables release (clearing settlement timing); the component-built FY0 owner FCF is ~S$610m (44.5% margin), and the FY1 projection is anchored to that, not to last_fcf. DATA VINTAGE WARNING: the extracted corpus ends at the FY2025 annual (June 2025). The H1 FY2026 (Dec-2025) and FY2026 (June-2026, released Aug-2026) filings are not in research/S68.SI/Extracted, so FY2026 - already reported - is modelled here as a forecast year and the balance sheet is 16 months old. The next refresh should load FY2026 and re-anchor base_revenue, net cash and the share count. Buybacks: S$26.3m FY2025 funds award vesting; the flat count is paid for.

bear.narrative: FY2025's record volumes prove cyclical: derivatives volumes mean-revert, Singapore cash-equities turnover slips back to its ~S$1.1bn/day decade average once the reform excitement fades, and falling SGD/USD short rates roughly halve the ~S$126m net treasury income on margin collateral (~4-5pp of margin). Competitive erosion in Asian index derivatives (HKEX MSCI A50 futures, NSE IX in GIFT City) caps pricing. Revenue flat-to-low growth, pre-SBC EBITDA margin slides to 58%, and capex stays elevated for the trading-platform upgrade.

base.narrative: FY2026 +8% (strong Singapore cash-equities ADV after the MAS equities-market review and record derivatives volumes, partly offset by lower SGD rates on treasury income), then mid-single-digit growth fading to 3% - in line with SGX's 5y revenue CAGR of 5.4%. Pre-SBC EBITDA margin held ~61.5-62.5% (FY2025 61.7%) with modest operating leverage.

bull.narrative: The MAS equities reforms (EQDP fund deployment, the SGX-Nasdaq dual-listing bridge, lower listing friction) revive Singapore cash-equities turnover structurally; FX futures and OTC FX (BidFX/MaxxTrader) compound as SGX becomes the Asian-hours FX venue; equity-derivatives (GIFT Connect, China A50, Asian index futures) keep taking share of risk-management flow. Revenue compounds 7-11% early on a largely fixed cost base, lifting pre-SBC EBITDA margin to 65%.

required_return_table.note: Each row rebuilds the terminal value at that row's rate (max(0, min(Gordon@r, 20x FCF_N))); the WACC row is valuation.base.intrinsic_value and the hurdle row is entry_price.base.entry_price.

sensitivity.note: Rows are WACC, columns terminal growth; each cell rebuilds its own terminal value.

probability_weighted.weights_rationale: Bear 20% (above the 15% default): FY2025 was a record volume year and treasury income is directly rate-exposed, so mean reversion from the starting base is a live risk, not a tail. Base 55%: SGX's decade of 4-6% revenue growth is unusually stable for an exchange. Bull 25% (below the 35% default): it needs both the MAS equity reforms to stick and FX/derivatives to keep compounding at high single digits - two independent things going right from an already-elevated base.

sanity_check.basis: SBC-adjusted on both sides (EPS less SBC/share; EBITDA less SBC), so these deliberately do not match GAAP screener multiples.
